A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniDomain work and contain 38 readable pages, including Appendices A–H. Complete text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching research content without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on 100 planning tasks and component ablations in Section 7, plus keyframe validation, per-class results and failure analyses in Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original planning evaluations, ablations, keyframe validation and failure analyses. Results retained from v2 remain original empirical results of this work.

M1.justification: Sections 3–6 retain identical energy-based keyframe extraction, closed-loop atomic-domain generation, hierarchical domain fusion and grounded PDDL planning procedures.

E1.justification: Both use DROID demonstrations, the BlockWorld, Desktop, Kitchen and Combination evaluation domains, and Agibot World for keyframe validation in Appendix D. No dataset or task scenario changes.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Code-as-Policies, ReAct, VLM-CoT, ISR-LLM, VLM-PDDL and BoN-iVML. Their documented adaptations in Appendix H are also identical.

E3.justification: Both retain the same 100-task evaluation, GPT-4.1 at temperature 0.0, SR/SPL/OR metrics and thresholds, teleoperation and human verification protocol, and baseline settings in Appendix H.

E4.justification: The domain-learning, fusion, grouping and filtering ablations in Figures 4–5 are identical. Appendix D's keyframe checks and Appendices E–F's case studies and failure analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report averages with standard errors in Figures 3–5 and 21. Neither provides different run or seed counts, statistical tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All plotted and stated results match, including 85% success and 83% optimality at K=0 in Section 7.2 and Figure 3. Ablation results, per-class comparisons and appendix failure-mode findings are identical.

T1.justification: The PDDL definitions, energy and solvability formulas, fusion and filtering mathematics, metric definitions, and Appendix D's Parseval-based reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about unified-domain pretraining, compositional zero-shot planning, and advantages over LLM-only and hybrid planners.

C2.justification: Performance interpretations and failure explanations are identical. Section 8 retains the same limitations concerning retrieval/fusion cost, PDDL 1.0 expressiveness and full observability.

D1.justification: Generation and fusion hyperparameters, Appendix D's keyframe window schedule, hardware and timing disclosures, prompts in Appendices G–H, and code/demo access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 55 reference entries are identical, preserving the same positioning against handcrafted domains, narrow-domain learning and external-feedback approaches.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v2, dated 26 Oct 2025, to v3, dated 20 Apr 2026. The displayed title, authors, prose, headings, section order and appendices are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–21, captions, axes, legends, boxed examples and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages match exactly except for the first-page version/date stamp wording.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the same scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations, reproducibility information and exposition throughout the main text and Appendices A–H. The administrative version/date update provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
